newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to buy 200,000 tonnes hard wheat in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to buy 200,000 tonnes hard wheat in 1997.

text.p: The Belarus government plans to buy 200,000 tonnes of hard wheat in 1997 against 500,000 tonnes of wheat purchased in 1996, the deputy chief of the Agriculture Ministry's crop division said on Friday.
"Belarus will buy hard varieties of wheat," Vyacheslav Herasimovich told Reuters. "This is the absolute minimum that Belarus will need for flour production."
Herasimovich said commercial companies might import more wheat into Belarus, which has forecast a grain harvest of 6.5 million tonnes this year compared to 5.8 million tonnes in 1996.
The Belarus Statistics Ministry said the former Soviet republic imported 1.2 million tonnes of grain last year compared to 650,000 tonnes in 1995.
